svg.text: goroutine lifecycle → channels/select → races/synchronization → patterns → project v.6

text.tspan: Process owns program resources.
Threads execute inside process.
Goroutines are scheduled by Go runtime.
Concurrency can interleave; parallelism is simultaneous.
Application exit ends remaining goroutines.
go statement starts concurrent work.
WaitGroup counts outstanding goroutines.
Add increments; Done decrements; Wait blocks.
Too many Add calls can deadlock.
Too many Done calls panic.
Typed conduit between goroutines.
Buffered channel exposes len/cap.
Directional types express producer/consumer roles.
close + comma-ok indicate completion state.
range waits until channel is closed.
select waits on multiple channel operations.
time.After implements timeout in source examples.
default is non-blocking but source calls it less safe.
select {} blocks forever.
nil channel disables that path by blocking forever.
Race = ordering-dependent shared-memory result.
go run -race reports conflicting accesses.
Mutex gives exclusive critical-section access.
RWMutex permits many readers but one writer.
Consistent lock ordering avoids deadlock examples.
sync/atomic provides indivisible operations.
AddInt64 / LoadInt64 power atomic counter example.
GOMAXPROCS limits simultaneous OS threads for Go code.
Source links default to logical CPU count.
Performance must be measured, not assumed.
Generator: lazy values.
Pipeline: staged transformations.
Queuing: N tasks across M goroutines.
Fan-in: many inputs → one output.
Fan-out: one input → many outputs.
Worker Pool: fixed worker group.
High difficulty adds parallel heuristic, limited minimax and zone analysis.
3×3 minimax candidate moves are also evaluated concurrently.
Each candidate uses copied board state to avoid races in source example.
Large-board win checks split row/column and diagonal work.
WaitGroup closes result channel after all checks finish.
SaveSnapshot / SaveFinishedGame run in background goroutines.
Load snapshots and finished games through result channels.
UI shows progress while DB operation is in flight.
Source notes snapshots could copy board state more rigorously.
Functional behavior remains same while blocking is reduced.

svg.text: Acceptance: explain goroutines/channels, detect races, choose synchronization, and map all six concurrency patterns.
Project acceptance: explain parallel AI evaluation, win checks and asynchronous persistence in v.6.
